children: Gold rebounded from its biggest weekly decline in eight months as traders scaled back bets on the Federal Reserve raising interest rates in the near term.

Bullion rose as much as 1.3% to around $3,582 an ounce, after falling 9% last week to a 14-month low. Traders are paring expectations of monetary tightening after growing concerns about artificial intelligence spending rippled across markets, sending technology stocks plunging.

Following the rout, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned the Fed risks jeopardizing the US economy by overtightening in response to latest inflation data. His prior attempt to rein in elevated long-term borrowing costs sent yields lower in August, which sparked a brief rally in gold.

Swaps traders are no longer fully pricing in a Fed rate hike in December after Treasury yields fell across the curve on Friday. The policy-sensitive two-year yields ended 12 basis points lower, a positive for non-yielding bullion.

Gold has fallen by an around a third since the US-Iran war erupted in late February as higher energy costs fueled inflation, prompting central banks to raise rates. It’s traded below the $4,000 support level since Nov. 11.

Spot gold rose 1.1% to $3,578.24 an ounce at 8:26 a.m. in Singapore, while silver was up 2.6% at $42.21 after tumbling 15% the week before. Platinum and palladium also advanced. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index dipped 0.1% after rising 0.6% last week.

title: Gold rebounds as traders pare bets on near-term Fed rate hikes
